verdicts.rewritten_summary: Human Dignity Trust profile (Malaysia, last updated 16 Dec 2025): same-sex 'carnal intercourse against the order of nature' is criminalised under Penal Code 1936 Sections 377A/377B with up to 20 years' imprisonment and whipping (Section 377D 'gross indecency' up to two years). It records a 28 November enforcement operation in Kuala Lumpur in which over 200 people were arrested at an all-male health centre by Kuala Lumpur police, Kuala Lumpur City Hall and the Federal Territories Islamic Religious Department (Jawi), and notes enforcement with arrests, prosecutions and corporal punishment since the 2018 election, with the Federal Court striking down some state Sharia criminal-code provisions as beyond state power.

Human Rights Watch/Justice for Sisters report (10 Aug 2022) documents state-sponsored discrimination against LGBT people in Malaysia based on interviews with 73 LGBT people between 2018 and 2021, including people living in Kuala Lumpur; it states that each state and the federal territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya have Sharia codes that typically criminalise same-sex conduct, and quotes a Kuala Lumpur activist describing regression as a conservative strand of Islam gains ground. It calls on lawmakers to decriminalise same-sex conduct and gender diversity.

Human Dignity Trust profile (Malaysia, last updated 16 Dec 2025) records that in November 2014 Malaysia's Court of Appeal declared section 66 of the Syariah Criminal Enactment 1992 (Negeri Sembilan), which criminalised cross-dressing, unconstitutional for breaching rights guaranteed by the Federal Constitution, and that the Federal Court has more recently struck down Sharia criminal-code provisions in Selangor and Kelantan because state legislatures lack criminal-law power. Federal criminalisation of same-sex conduct persists under Penal Code 1936 Sections 377A/377B (up to 20 years' imprisonment with whipping), with a crackdown involving arrests, prosecutions and corporal punishment since the 2018 election.

Human Rights Watch/Justice for Sisters report (10 Aug 2022) documents state-sponsored discrimination and criminalisation of LGBT people in Malaysia, based on interviews with 73 people between 2018 and 2021 including people living in Negeri Sembilan; it states that every state and the federal territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya have Sharia codes that typically criminalise same-sex conduct. It calls on lawmakers to decriminalise same-sex conduct and gender diversity and to abandon 'rehabilitation' programs and rhetoric.
